explanation: Hebrew, Persian and Urdu scripts also run right to left. Numbers are the exception: in Arabic text, multi-digit numbers are still read from left to right.

claims.text: Arabic script is written from right to left.
Arabic script is not written left to right or top to bottom.
Hebrew script and the Arabic-based scripts of Persian and Urdu are also written right to left.
Multi-digit numbers in Arabic text read from left to right.

writerNotes: Two distractors on purpose: bottom to top would be filler. The number fact surprises even people who know the direction. evidence.restatement: Arabic script is written from right to left.
Arabic is not written left to right or top to bottom.
Hebrew script, and the Arabic-based scripts of Persian and Urdu, also run right to left.
In Arabic text, numbers are written with the most significant digit on the left, so their digits run left to right.

issues.note: Explanation and c4 say numbers are 'read' left to right. That is true of the written order of digits, but spoken Arabic puts units before tens (25 is 'five and twenty'), so 'written' would be more exact than 'read'.
